events.credibility_reason: The report itself says some listed results were mis-formalised or trivial versions; Tao says the misformalised version of 418 was likely what was proved; the list contains at least one acknowledged error.

why: The statement asks only whether an odd noncototient exists. Every even-side result (Browkin–Schinzel, Flammenkamp–Luca, Grytczuk–Mędryk, González et al., Banks–Luca counts, Pomerance–Yang densities) answers a neighbouring question about infinitude or density of noncototients and is scored variant. The Cloitre OEIS comment and the Lean conditional variant only reduce the question to an unproven strong-Goldbach statement, so they are none. Semchankau gives an asymptotic count with no existence conclusion for any odd c, so it is none too. The Alexeev formalisation re-proves a 1995 even-side theorem: it is a formalisation of known results, so none. ChatGPT only explained that proof, so its AI role is none as well. The 2026 Lean statement of the odd conjecture proves nothing. Seed-Prover's claim concerns Erdős #418 (infinitude), not the odd question, so it is variant; it is marked generated for its own event by its quote and doubtful because of the misformalisation dispute. No event exhibits an odd noncototient or proves that none exists.
doubts: The researcher's own derivation that odd noncototients have density zero, via almost-all Goldbach, is not in any source, so it was not scored. Even if it were, it would be density information that does not answer the existence question.
